item.title: Blue Öyster Cult at American Music Theatre — Fri Aug 21, 8:00 PM — American Music Theatre
item.description: For more than five decades, Blue Öyster Cult has thrilled audiences around the world with its signature blend of intelligent hard rock and heavy metal. Widely regarded as one of the genre’s most influential bands, BÖC has earned both critical acclaim and commercial success—an achievement few of their peers can claim. Their innovative sound and thought-provoking lyrics have inspired generations of artists, including bands like Metallica. From their self-titled debut in 1972 to today, Blue Öyster Cult has built a legendary catalog of music that balances power, melody, and mystique. Fans can expect to hear iconic hits like “(Don’t Fear) The Reaper,” “Godzilla,” and “Burnin’ for You,” along with a deep lineup of fan favorites including “Cities on Flame with Rock and Roll,” “Astronomy,” and “Veteran of the Psychic Wars.” Still touring relentlessly, the band continues to deliver electrifying live performances that showcase their enduring appeal and musicianship. item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Aug 24, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Indigenous Peoples and the American Revolution: The Sullivan Expedition of 1779 — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — Historic Rock Ford
item.description:
Historic Rock Ford’s Untold Stories of the American Revolution Lecture Series welcomes Mary Ann Levine as she presents “Indigenous Peoples and the American Revolution: The Sullivan Expedition of 1779.”
In the late summer of 1779, under direct orders from George Washington, General John Sullivan led an army of several thousand men on a campaign against the Six Nations of the Haudenosaunee. The goal of the campaign was to break the confederacy’s ability to support and supply British forces by destroying food stores, burning villages, and driving the Haudenosaunee out of both Pennsylvania and New York. During the Sullivan expedition and its aftermath, an estimated 50%-60% of the Haudenosaunee died from direct military violence, disease, starvation, and exposure. In the early 20th century, dozens of memorials to the Sullivan campaign were erected over hundreds of miles of Sullivan’s march.

item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Aug 23, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
